summary: Pre-prod smoke sweep for NivXRay (v1.3.x). Verified login, nav tabs, dropdowns, /battery page contents, PREDICT TREE (no 502 in first run), workspace primary buttons. Discovered two P0 issues: (1) backend event-loop hang caused by L3 LLM dispatcher blocking pattern in llm_decoder.py, (2) /battery route missing top Header - users lose global navigation once on that route. Backend became unresponsive twice during the test run and required supervisor restart to recover.

critical.issue: Event loop appears to hang after prolonged use. `curl /api/health` times out (HTTP=000). netstat shows Recv-Q accumulating on port 8001. Coincides with repeating log line `L3: dispatch failed:` (empty exception). Requires `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` to recover. Root cause in /app/backend/llm_decoder.py:119-122 — `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(..., loop).result(timeout=..)` blocks a worker thread on the same running event loop; under sustained decode traffic, the default FastAPI threadpool (~40 workers) all end up blocked waiting on futures whose coroutines can't be scheduled → deadlock. The empty exception is likely a TimeoutError with no message. Reproduced twice.

minor.issue: log.warning('L3: dispatch failed: %s', e) with empty str(e) — unhelpful for debugging. Should log repr(e) or traceback.

ui_bugs.issue: Page does NOT import or render <Header />. Users navigating to /battery lose the top-nav completely (WORKSPACE / BATCH / HEATMAP / BENCHMARK / BATTERY / TOOLS / LEARN / ADMIN tabs all disappear). Cannot navigate away without editing URL. Confirmed via source (`grep -n Header /app/frontend/src/pages/MultiLayerBatteryPage.jsx` → no match) and via runtime check (`[data-testid=nav-workspace]` absent on /battery).
React key-prop warning: 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop' — check render method of ThreatIntelAdminPanel.

integration_issues.issue: Could not verify due to backend hang mid-run. Sample fills, click succeeds, but backend did not respond within 40s window on the failed run. First-attempt run confirmed the button is wired and produces network activity but AI response was not returned in time (may need >30s cold-path). Retest after backend fix required.

If called from an async request path, `await _call_claude(...)` directly with `asyncio.wait_for`. If called from sync path (threadpool), keep as-is but ensure worker thread count is not exhausted by decode traffic (or move L3 to a fully-async path).

rca_of_the_issue: Backend deadlock RCA: /app/backend/llm_decoder.py L3 helper detects a running event loop (line 116), then submits the Claude coroutine to that loop via `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe` and BLOCKS on `.result(timeout=_TIMEOUT_S+2)`. When this helper is called from a coroutine running on that same loop, the submitted coroutine cannot progress until the caller yields, but the caller is blocked on `.result()` — hard deadlock, only broken by the timeout. Even from threadpool workers, under sustained decode traffic every worker ends up parked on `.result()` and the pool exhausts, so all subsequent sync-path requests (including /api/health, which itself is fast) queue behind Starlette's threadpool. netstat Recv-Q>0 confirms the accepted connections are never being read. Empty `str(e)` in the log line = TimeoutError. Mitigation: (1) if called from async context, `await asyncio.wait_for(_call_claude(...), timeout=_TIMEOUT_S)` instead of round-tripping through the loop; (2) if a sync entrypoint is truly required, run the coroutine on a DIFFERENT (dedicated) event loop in its own thread, not the request loop.
